articles.title: Pierpaolo Piccioli presents ‘most personal show’ at Balenciaga
articles.summary: Italian designer imbues collection with signature flourishes and style rooted in the craft of the couture atelier. It was “the most personal show I have done here”, the designer Pierpaolo Piccioli said after his Balenciaga presentation at Paris fashion week on Thursday.
body: Piccioli, who always wears a coral necklace, placed a monumental sculpture of undersea coral crafted from fabric in the middle of the catwalk. Like Cristóbal Balenciaga, Piccioli is both a maximalist and a minimalist. He likes boldness but not fuss, each look one audacious idea executed cleanly. A floor-length ivory cape fastened with a simple gold clasp. A black suit with one bold slash of tangerine at the jacket hem. A gown covered from neck to ankle in bubbles of organza.

“I like surfaces to be either entirely embellished or super clean,” he said. He loves colour for how instinctively we react to it, because “how you feel in your clothes is much more important than how you look in them”.

A year into the job, Piccioli has his reasons to feel the need to stake Balenciaga’s territory as his own. He used the show to remind the Paris audience that his way of making clothes, which is rooted in the craft of the couture atelier rather than in contemporary obsessions with branding and virality and the attention economy, is what Cristobal himself would have wanted for his house.
points: Italian designer imbues collection with signature flourishes and style rooted in the craft of the couture atelier.

articles.title: Terrible idea or major coup? Galliano’s Zara collection launches after Met controversy
articles.summary: Collaboration regarded as ‘really big thing’ for retailer in some quarters despite backlash around designer’s antisemitic remarks in 2011. A month after it was announced that a planned exhibition dedicated to fashion designer John Galliano at New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art would not proceed…
body: Called Re{form}, it was, according to a press release, “authored by the couturier John Galliano. Built from our memory. Made for now.”

Its launch in shops comes after controversy over plans to honour the former Dior designer, who was found guilty of a hate crime in 2011 after a series of racist and antisemitic rants, with an exhibition of his work at the Met and a corresponding Met gala – a juggernaut of popular culture viewed by billions globally online. The exhibition was cancelled but had it gone ahead, it would have been only the third time such an honour had been bestowed on a living designer. The only others being Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo of Comme des Garçons in 2017.

The backlash to the plans were vehement and widespread, with Met patrons, New York politicians and prominent Jewish leaders objecting. Writing in the New York Times, his biographer Dana Thomas labelled it a “terrible idea”, saying that “choosing this moment to glorify the life’s work of someone who was convicted of making antisemitic remarks … is downright bizarre”, and noting that “his infamous antisemitic rants were not an aberration”.

articles.title: My wife obsessively consumes US news. She’s so stressed but can’t turn off. What should I do? | Leading questions
articles.summary: Instead of asking her to step away from her distress, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith, could you suggest she channel it into action? My wife is obsessed with everything that’s happening in the US.
body: I’ve told her she needs to take at least one day off all social media, but she won’t do that even for an hour. It stresses her out more and more every day, but she just keeps going back to it – and it has been really affecting me, more lately than ever. On weekends I stay up late playing games (my way of winding down after a week of work) and she’ll go to bed early. And during those times sometimes I just sit and cry. Everything that’s happening is so stressful, and there’s nothing we can do about it. I just wish I could rip away her phone and let her breathe! I don’t know what to say or do. Is there anything that could help?

Eleanor says: It’s so easy to feel that if you’re a politically engaged person you have to stay tuned in and upset. The general collapse of everything is distressing. So it can seem like an obligation of responsible citizenship to be distressed.

articles.title: 'It’s a little splurge that adds a lot of joy': 22 whimsical products that make us smile
articles.summary: When life starts to feel boring, a touch of levity is just what the doctor ordered. Our contributors’ picks make even work and cleaning feel playful. A buckwheat pillow and 10lb blanket: what you loved most in September.
body: Welcome to Filter finds, a series where Filter contributors share the things they love most – and think you might, too.

The objects we choose to surround ourselves with should, above all, be useful – but life is short. Why not have a little fun while we’re at it? This month, we asked our contributors to share the practical things that spark not only joy, but whimsy – a sense of playfulness in our everyday lives. They certainly delivered!
From a toilet brush shaped like Excalibur to a concrete banana, these are the items our contributors use in pursuit of a whimsical life.

A couple in my town have installed some goose decoys in their front yard and dress them up thematically to delight passersby. And I am definitely delighted when I drive by and look to see what the “Nelsonville geese” are doing. They get dressed for holidays such as St Paddy’s Day, Cinco de Mayo (drinking Coronas), Fourth of July... and they have a Santa sleigh. They also do local things such as fishing in a baby pool to coincide with the local fish and game club’s fishing derby. They are hikers with trash strewn around their feet (a local peeve). During Covid, they social-distanced, 6ft apart.

articles.title: Sarah Jessica Parker’s Gray-Blended Updo is Exquisite
articles.summary: The actor wore a Simone Rocha sheer gown, along with a matching ribbon in her almost knee-length hair, for a special event at the New York City Ballet.
body: Sarah Jessica Parker is in peak form during ballet season. And tonight, the actor arrived on the red carpet for the New York City Ballet’s Fall Fashion Gala (she’s a founding member of the event) in romantic, ribboned fashion.

For the occasion, Parker chose a floral, sheer gown by Simone Rocha for the occasion, and styled her hair to match. Her long hair—typically worn in beachy waves—was instead pulled back into a Rapunzel-esque updo (extensions helped it reach almost to her knees!). From there, her hairstylist wove a pink ribbon through the hair the perfectly matched those on her gown.

Parker’s longtime colorist, Gina Gilbert at Benjamin Salon, has been working with the star for years to transition her sunny blonde into something gray-friendly. Using a technique called “gray blending,” Gilbert melds bright highlights and natural gray hair into a seamless look.
Parker isn’t the only star who’s stepped out this week with their gray on full display: at the Zurich Film Festival, actor Olivia Colman made a chic case for quitting dye with her silver curls.

articles.title: Nike Announces Layoffs, Operating Changes as Q1 Sales Fall Further
articles.summary: Nike shares fell another 6% after the company reported a 5% revenue dip in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, missing expectations. Nike introduced a new program, Pace, which will involve layoffs.
body: “For the first quarter, results were in line with our expectation. Last fiscal year, we grew the [Nike brand performance portfolio] business to $16 billion. We built on that foundation this quarter, growing Nike performance by another high-single digits,” president and CEO Elliott Hill told investors on Thursday’s call. “Despite that progress, our Nike performance business is not yet large enough to offset the pressure we're seeing in Nike sportswear, Jordan brand, and greater China. We’re taking deliberate actions to strengthen those businesses, but realizing the full benefit of those efforts will take time.”

Hill also welcomed new CFO Dave Denton, who joined the company on August 17. “Dave brings deep financial expertise, strong operational leadership, and a proven track record of helping world-class companies grow,” he said.

articles.title: What Is a Neuro-Wellness Spa Retreat—and Why Are Travelers Flocking to Them?
articles.summary: A travel writer with a family history of Alzheimer’s disease grapples with the wellness trend of neurological optimization that aims to make the mind sharper—and perhaps less disease-prone.
body: I arrived at Palace Merano, the storied wellness getaway in South Tyrol near the Italian Dolomites, utterly famished. After an early-morning flight to Venice, followed by a four-hour drive, I want to collapse in my room almost as much as I want a snack. Once I get to my room I’m dreaming of raiding the mini bar or devouring a complimentary fruit basket when I look around to see—nothing. No nectarines or oranges or grapes, no tray of sweets; I thrust open the doors of the armoire, but all I see is a large bottle of mineral water and a selection of caffeine-free herbal teas. There’s even no coffee machine, let alone coffee.
points: A travel writer with a family history of Alzheimer’s disease grapples with the wellness trend of neurological optimization that aims to make the mind sharper—and perhaps less disease-prone.

articles.title: Venus Retrograde 2026 Is Coming—Here’s What It Means for Every Star Sign
articles.summary: Think of Venus retrograde, which runs from October 3 to November 13, as a steamy, scandalous romance novel that fuels our passions and liaisons. Read on for our astrologer’s full breakdown by zodiac sign of what the Venus retrograde 2026 signifies.
body: Think of Venus retrograde in Scorpio and Libra, from October 3 to November 13, as a steamy, scandalous romance novel that fuels our passions and liaisons. The planet of love and desire is slowing down, rewriting the next chapters more deliberately. Venus retrograde, which happens every 18 to 19 months, is a check-in to make sure we are growing and receiving tenderness. Yes, it’s going to be messy and dramatic—unions will be on and off for the next 40 days and 40 nights. It’s breakup and makeup season.

A few noteworthy themes arise from this retrograde. First, Venus in Scorpio and Mars in Leo abruptly link up on October 10 under the New Moon in Libra, pushing us to chase love. The cat-and-mouse game intensifies, urging us to figure out what we truly crave from commitments. Do we want to play games, or do we want a secure foundation? The choice is yours.

articles.title: Why You Shouldn't Expect a Tiny Kindle Any Time Soon
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Earlier this week, I commented that the recent boom in tiny e-readers—I'm talking about those credit card-sized, Chinese-made e-ink devices that have become all the rage on BookTok and Reddit —was the most interesting thing to happen to the market…
body: While it's monitoring the chatter around devices like the Palma or even smaller options like the X4 Pro, for Amazon, the existing entry-level Kindle is "a really good format," Keith said. "Getting to four or five inches, I think there's just a lot of compromises there that you have to make. The core answer is just making a better entry device."

Chris Green, Kindle's vice president of design, a veteran who has worked on every Kindle device save the first-generation model (which was released just as he joined the company), agreed, while leaving the door open just a crack wider: "I think they're fascinating," Green said of smaller alternative e-readers, while admitting they weren't for him (he prefers to read on a massive Kindle Scribe). "Are we going to do one? I don't know. Are we looking into them? Yes."

What does "looking into them" mean? Well, "we look into everything," he said, noting Amazon has previously investigated both foldable and rollable e-readers. "But those things are fascinating," he added. "I don't know if [they're] going to be successful, but [they're] definitely worth watching."

body: In the spirit of sorting out what is worth visiting, this list includes 38 restaurants and experiences for first-time and seasoned diners in Mexico City, focusing on projects that have distinctive culinary point of views, clear commitments to hospitality, and/or young local talent in the kitchen.

We update this list regularly to make sure it reflects the ever-changing Mexico City dining scene. Our write-ups include insider tips from our experienced writers and editors, as well as a rough range of pricing for each destination — ranging from $ for quick, inexpensive meals with dishes largely under $10 (or the equivalent in pesos), to $$$$ for places where entrees exceed $30.
